messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager duty triggered — GPU pool 'rt-gpu-eu-1' queue depth > 95th percentile and sustained for 4m. Severity: P1. Paging oncall: Amanda (oncall). Link: https://pager.redwood.example/incidents/2815567890
Amanda (oncall): I got it, joining bridge now. Starting quick triage — what's the visible impact?
Deepak: Seeing queue length spike on rt-gpu-eu-1, requests queued up, autoscaler didn't add new nodes. Error rate: 8% 5xx on generation routes.
Sophie: Also seeing lots of driver XID 13/31 errors in node logs, frequent GPU resets. That will reduce effective capacity.
Amanda (oncall): On bridge: https://zoom.redwood.example/j/2815567890. Can someone paste top errors?
Mike: Logs from node gpu-node-23: ```Mar 15 12:14:32 gpu-driver[pid]: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1): 31, PID 4321 ```
Julia: And OOM traces around the same time: ```kworker: runtime oom: process llm-server pid=4321 killed by OOM```. Nodes report memory pressure and occasional flapping (kube node Ready->NotReady).
Deepak: Autoscaler metrics show scale_attempts=3 but failures due to instance provisioning timeouts and a quota throttling error: ```QuotaExceeded: Could not allocate new GPU instance (limit=12)```
Amanda (oncall): So root causes: driver/runtime instability causing effective capacity loss + cloud quota preventing autoscale. Impacting hosted customers in EU region. Need immediate mitigation to reduce customer impact.
Sophie: Short-term options: 1) divert new traffic away from rt-gpu-eu-1 via routing policy, 2) fallback to smaller model variants for non-critical tiers, 3) force drain problematic nodes and restart driver service.
Amanda (oncall): Agreed. Start with routing change and model fallback. Deepak, can you push a temporary routing policy to move new sessions to rt-gpu-ap-1 and rt-gpu-us-2?
Deepak: On it. Applying policy: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/routing/policies -d '{"name":"emergency-eu-shift","match":{"region":"eu"},"targets":["rt-gpu-ap-1","rt-gpu-us-2"],"mode":"failover"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'```
Deepak: Policy applied, starting to drain new traffic from rt-gpu-eu-1. Old sessions will continue for 10m.
Amanda (oncall): Sophie, can we enable model-fallback for standard and free tiers? Reduce CPU/GPU load by switching to quantized / q4 variants.
Sophie: Yes toggling fallback via console: route-mapping update done — non-SLA routes now hit q4f variants. Expect ~30-50% throughput improvement per GPU.
Mike: Meanwhile I'm cordoning gpu-node-23 and gpu-node-27, draining pods, and restarting nvidia-driver on both. Command: ```kubectl cordon gpu-node-23 && kubectl drain gpu-node-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data```
Mike: Restarting drivers: ```systemctl restart nvidia-driver.service```
infra-bot: Node gpu-node-23 marked unschedulable by Mike at 12:23 UTC.
Julia: Quick health snapshot: queue_depth=820 -> after routing change dropped to 240 in 3m. 5xx rate dropping from 8% -> 2.1%. Good improvement.
Deepak: Cloud quota request in progress with provider, raised to support for expedited increase. Reference ticket: CLOUD-QUOTA-9876. Provisioning failures should stop once quota cleared. ETA ~45m per provider response.
Amanda (oncall): For customers affected, open interim status note. Sophie please draft. We should mention degraded performance and model fallbacks, no data loss, engineers working on recovery.
Sophie: Draft posted to status.redwood.example: "Reduced capacity in EU region caused elevated latency and generation errors. Traffic shifted to alternate regions and smaller model variants for non-critical tiers. Working on driver restarts and quota increase. No customer data lost." Link: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/2815567890
Deepak: Noting repeated Xid sequences — pushing driver stacktrace from gpu-node-23: ```GPU fault: Xid 13 at kernel module nvml->nvlink; trace: 0x7f2a...; klog snippet: gpu_reset called 12 times in 8m```
Amanda (oncall): That suggests hardware-level resets or a bad driver/kernel combo. Mike, after restart, monitor for recurrence and report GPU reset counts.
Mike: Restart completed at 12:29 UTC. gpu-reset-count before=12, after=0 (initial). Rejoining node to cluster. ```kubectl uncordon gpu-node-23```
infra-bot: Node gpu-node-23 Ready at 12:33 UTC.
Julia: Metrics look stabilizing but still seeing small flares. Queue depth now ~180 and decreasing. 5xx ~1.2%.
Sophie: Can we enable autoscaler override to temporarily raise max nodes beyond quota while cloud ticket pending? Might bypass but requires manual approval (ops lead).
Amanda (oncall): Ops lead approval granted via DM. Deepak, apply override to max_pool_size=20 for rt-gpu-eu-1 for next 60m.
Deepak: Override applied. Autoscaler will retry provisioning. If provisioning still fails due to hard quota, it will log quota errors but attempt.
Mike: After driver restart, Xid errors dropped. I still see two nodes flapping earlier; pulled kubelet logs showing intermittent kernel oops. Suspecting a kernel patch mismatch on older image.
Sophie: Good catch. We'll schedule a rolling kernel-driver compatibility patchpack. For now pin workloads away from older nodes by setting nodeSelector to new-image nodes.
Amanda (oncall): Action items: - Deepak: monitor autoscale & cloud ticket (CLOUD-QUOTA-9876) - Mike: keep watch on node resets; collect driver logs and node histograms - Sophie: coordinate fallback & status updates - Julia: track customer error windows and map to accounts impacted
Deepak: Autoscaler retries succeeded for 2 additional nodes at 12:41 UTC; new capacity added. However one provisioning attempt failed due to quota, second succeeded because it used a different SKU.
Julia: Customer impact summary so far: 22 customers saw increased latency, 5 customers had timeouts; highest severity customers rerouted before session loss.
Amanda (oncall): Let's keep incident open for monitoring and follow-up — set postmortem owners: Deepak (lead), Sophie (mitigation), Mike (root cause logs). I'll update with timeline.
Sophie: Postmortem template created: https://docs.redwood.example/postmortems/2815567890. Adding notes to TL;DR: driver instability + quota exhaustion -> autoscaler unable to fully recover -> routing and fallbacks mitigated customer impact.
Mike: Uploading driver logs bundle to S3: s3://redwood-incidents/2815567890/driver-logs.tar.gz
infra-bot: Incident updated to status 'mitigated' at 13:05 UTC by Amanda (oncall).
Amanda (oncall): Marking the thread as handoff to oncall follow-up. If anything regresses, re-ping #incidents. Great work team :thumbsup:
